newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO blames Israeli hardline policies for violence.
newsitem.headline: PLO blames Israeli hardline policies for violence.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Thursday that Israel brought a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem on itself through hardline policies which were frustrating peace efforts.

"Israeli attempts to lay the blame on the Palestinian Authority are rejected. Israel is responsible for feeding extremism on both sides by freezing the peace process and by continuously violating agreements," said Nabil Abu Rdainah, an adviser to President Yasser Arafat.
Two Arab suicide bombers, believed to be from the militant Islamic group Hamas, killed 13 people in an attack on Wednesday in the Mahane Yehuda market in the heart of Jewish west Jerusalem.
Israel accused the Palestinian Authority, in charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, of not doing enough to stop Moslem militants.
Mohammad Dahlan, chief of the Palestinian Preventive Security agency in Gaza, said the Israeli government's hardline policies created an atmosphere which motivated militants to carry out attacks.

"We are against the attacks and we condemn them strongly, but the irresponsible policies of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu and his government are responsible for the attacks," Dahlan told Reuters.

"Netanyahu's policies have driven the Palestinians to a state of despair and frustration by seizing their lands, building settlements and refusing to implement peace deals," he said. "Israel must understand that to have security, peace and stability must prevail."
PLO officials had repeatedly warned that Israel's settlement building, which led to a suspension of formal peace talks in March, was an explosive move.
Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and prevented the movement of Palestinians between their villages and cities in the wake of Wednesday's double bombing.
PLO officials condemned the closure as collective punishment which they said would increase hostility towards Israel and lead to more violence.

Arafat ordered his security forces to crack down on militants suspected of involvement in the bombings. Hamas claimed responsibility for the attacks in a leaflet faxed to an international news agency.
Three PLO-Israeli security meetings took place late on Wednesday in the West Bank to discuss security matters after the bombings, officials said.

PLO security chiefs said they would not make mass arrests merely to please Israel but would detain only those who they believed were linked to the attacks. They said they still were still not certain which political group was behind the bombings.
Netanyahu's communications adviser David Bar-Illan said Israel might re-enter PLO-ruled areas in order to seize "terrorists" if the Palestinian police failed to do the job themselves.
Late on Wednesday, Netanyahu's security cabinet decided against pursuing talks with the Palestinians until the Authority moved against the militants.
Abu Rdainah said Arafat summoned consuls general of Western states and demanded immediate international intervention to stop Israel's "dangerous cabinet decisions".
PLO security chief Jibril Rajoub warned Israel against going back into Palestinian areas it handed over in 1994 in line with the peace accords.
"The Palestinians and the Authority will do everything to defend their land," he said.
